label: late original-phase s/v/t/q/w/k input in a sequence that began with h/o/r/3/0/j
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at t>=3, peaking at t=4-6 (97% of mass in the original phase, about 3% on the <DEL> step, essentially none during copying). It depends on the current input token: s is strongest (8.8x lift, 36% of mass, every top example is on s), then v and t, then q/w/k. It also depends on which tokens came earlier: activation is higher when the sequence starts with h/o/r/3/0/j (first_tok lift about 3x). It is mostly on first occurrences of the input token. The rule looks graded and conjunctive (current token x earlier context), so a boolean predicate only partly captures it: dev precision about 0.30, recall 0.60, mass recall 0.72. Precision is limited because s/v/t inputs with h/o/r-type openings often stay below threshold. Misses are mostly weak activations on other tokens (digits, y, u, p, <DEL>) that share the same history. Does not fire at t<2 or in the copy phase.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=v (+3.50), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=s (+2.57), phase=0 & in_tok=s (+2.57), orig0=o (+2.52), phase=0 & in_tok=q (+2.36), orig0=h (+2.28). Lower it: phase=2 (-6.43), orig0=s (-4.66), prev3_tok=- (-4.66), orig0=u (-4.50).
